title: Monotonicity of output probability
statement: Let $r$ be a function from finite Boolean words to either an output in a set $\alpha$ or no output, and suppose that once $r$ outputs a value, appending any Boolean word leaves that output unchanged. For any output $v\in\alpha$ and natural numbers $t\le t'$, the probability that $r$ outputs $v$ on a uniformly random Boolean word of length $t$ is at most the corresponding probability for a uniformly random Boolean word of length $t'$.
hypotheses_covered: $r$ is prefix-stable: an output persists after appending any word
